'''Sara Cosette Billey''' is an American mathematician working in [[algebraic combinatorics]]. She is known for her contributions on [[Schubert polynomial]]s, singular loci of [[Schubert varieties]], [[Kostant polynomial]]s, and [[Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial]]s<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/mathscinet/MRAuthorID/341999|title=Billey, Sara C.|website=MathSciNet|language=en|access-date=2017-04-10}}</ref> often using computer verified proofs. She is currently a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Washington]].<ref name=cv/>

== Education and career ==
Billey did her undergraduate studies at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], graduating in 1990.<ref name=cv>{{cite web|url=https://www.math.washington.edu/~billey/cv.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae|date=September 26, 2017|accessdate=2018-04-30}}</ref>
She earned her Ph.D. in mathematics in 1994 from the [[University of California, San Diego]], under the joint supervision of [[Adriano Garsia]] and [[Mark Haiman]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=39979}}</ref> She returned to MIT as a postdoctoral researcher with [[Richard P. Stanley]], and continued there as an assistant and associate professor until 2003, when she moved to the University of Washington.<ref name=cv/>

==Recognition==
In 2000, Billey received the [[Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers]], the highest honor given by the United States government to mathematicians, scientists, and engineers near the start of their independent research careers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/honorary-awards/pecase/recipients/sara-c-billey|website=US National Science Foundation | department=PECASE recipients |title=Sara C. Billey|access-date=August 17, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |volume=48|issue=2|title=Mathematics People {{!}} PECASE Awards Announced|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/200102/200102FullIssue.pdf?adat=February%202001&trk=&cat=none&type=.pdf|access-date=August 17, 2026}}</ref>  Billey became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2012, in the inaugural class.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society|publisher=American Mathematical Society|accessdate=July 31, 2015| archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626101726/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|archivedate=June 26, 2015}}</ref>
